Tess (Support): Hey team — Acme App reported 5xx spikes and timeouts on hosted inference starting ~09:04 UTC. They see a lot of gateway errors (502/504) and some requests hanging for >30s. They attached a few example request IDs. Can infra/sre triage?

Acme App (customer): seeing ~15% errors on our production traffic, started abruptly. We rolled no code. Response body: "upstream timeout" and occasional "cache lookup failed". Our app is blocked for customers.

Ravi (Infra): Noted. I'm checking Redis metrics and our cache fleet right now. Any correlation to deploys?

Tess (Support): No deploys from the customer. Our console shows a small config push to cache-client lib at 08:50 but that was a canary. Not sure if related.

Maya (SRE): Paging @oncall via deploy-bot... deploy-bot: Incident created #INC-2026-1782.

Ravi (Infra): Looking at redis-prod cluster 3/5 nodes show elevated CPU and >1k blocked clients. Miss ratio spiked and eviction rate shot up at 09:03 UTC. Could be a thrash/eviction storm.

Jon (Platform): Any recent change to prefix caching or a TTL policy? Optimize tool suggested lowering TTLs yesterday for LLM KV caching.

Ravi (Infra): I see a config rollout to cache policy for prefix-sync at 08:48 (affected subset). The agent changed default maxmemory-policy from volatile-lru -> allkeys-lru, which would increase evictions across the board. Rolling back to previous policy might stabilize.

Maya (SRE): Error patterns from the API: most 5xx are 502/gateway_timeout from our edge, with backend timings showing large queuing inside the model server waiting on KV fetchs. Logs: 
```
[09:04:12] model-srv-03 - WARN - kv.fetch timeout 30000ms for prefix: user-embedding/abc123
[09:04:12] api-gateway - ERROR - upstream error: cache-proxy: upstream timeout
[09:04:13] model-srv-04 - ERROR - failed to get kv: redis timeout after 1 attempt
```
Tess (Support): Customer attached a few request IDs we can use for repro. They sent traffic at 09:02-09:10 UTC.

Ravi (Infra): I'm doing an immediate config rollback on the prefix cache policy for the affected pool. Rolling config to previous policy now (targeting redis-prod/*). I'll also throttle cache client concurrency to reduce blocked_clients.

Maya (SRE): Recommend also enabling fail-open for prefix cache on model server (short-circuit to compute if cache returns error) — we have runbook step for that. If the model server can bypass cache, it will reduce backend queuing at cost of higher token compute.

Jon (Platform): I'm preparing a quick hotfix to add a short-circuit TTL fallback within the cache client (300ms deadline) to avoid long waits. If we can't push client change fast, we can flip a feature flag to fail-open at runtime.

Ravi (Infra): Rollback applied at 09:12 UTC to maxmemory-policy=volatile-lru for the affected shards. I'm also restarting the busiest redis instances one-at-a-time to clear blocked clients and free memory (rolling restart).

Maya (SRE): After the rollback and first restart, we see blocked_clients drop from ~1k to ~120 and CPU start to normalize. API 5xx rate reduced from 14% -> 4% within 3 minutes.

Tess (Support): I told Acme App we were rolling a config rollback and will follow up in 15m with status. They asked for a postmortem and recommended mitigations.

Acme App (customer): Thanks — we're seeing errors drop now. Please keep us posted. We need a short post-incident note for our on-call.

Ravi (Infra): Completed rolling restart by 09:20 UTC. Metrics look healthy: miss ratio stable, evictions back to baseline. P99 redis latency dropped to sub-3ms.

Maya (SRE): Mitigations applied: config rollback, rolling restarts, throttle on client concurrency, enabled fail-open flag on model staging (will push to prod if stable). Creating follow-up TODOs: add circuit-breaker on cache client, perf test for high eviction scenarios, and an alert on blocked_clients > 500.

Jon (Platform): I'll add a runtime feature flag to enable short-circuit fallback for prefix KV requests and a knob to set client deadline (default 300ms). Also putting a guard in the optimizer that avoids lowering TTLs automatically for heavy prefix caches without a safety check.

Tess (Support): Action items I captured for the customer: 1) Postmortem + timeline, 2) Mitigation steps we took, 3) Temporary recommendation: enable model server fail-open or increase margin for compute, 4) Request they avoid sudden traffic spikes during config tuning.

Maya (SRE): Postmortem draft outline: timeline, root cause = config rollout changed redis eviction policy leading to eviction storm + blocked clients -> KV timeouts -> API gateway 502/504; contributing factor = no circuit-breaker on cache client and low client deadlines. Next steps: implement circuit breaker, add blocked_clients alert, default safe TTLs, and add canary gating for cache policy changes.

Ravi (Infra): I'll link Redis config change PR and the canary job output to the postmortem. Also adding a remediation playbook entry for forced rollback when blocked_clients > 300 and 5xx% > 5% within 10m.

Tess (Support): Thanks everyone. I'll update the customer in 20m with the incident summary. If anyone wants to be on the postmortem call at 11:00 UTC, ping me. :thumbsup:

Maya (SRE): Adding owners for follow-ups: Ravi (infra) -> config guard + alerting, Jon (platform) -> client fail-open flag + circuit-breaker, Tess (support) -> customer comms + postmortem.

Ravi (Infra): One more note — we should consider making prefixed LRU changes behind a feature flag that can be toggled without full rollout; current rollout mechanism applied to too broad a set.

Tess (Support): Closing thread for now, will reopen if errors creep back. Thanks all.
